w: Stanislas Leszczynski, deposed King of Poland turned Duke of Lorraine, ordered this pedestrianised square raised between 1752 and 1756 to link the old town to the new. It stands today as one of the finest examples of 18th-century urban design in Europe, and has carried UNESCO World Heritage status since 1983.
s: An 18th-century royal square for an ousted king
_facts: Built 1752-1756 on the orders of Stanislas Leszczynski, former King of Poland and Duke of Lorraine
One of the oldest examples of an architecturally consistent monumental public square
Part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983, with Place de la Carriere and Place d'Alliance

w: Tucked into one of the pavilions ringing the Place Stanislas, this is among the oldest museums in France, its collection of European paintings running from old masters into modern design -- including a room devoted to Nancy's own Art Nouveau glassmaker Daum and the designer Jean Prouve.
s: One of France's oldest museums, on the royal square
_facts: One of the oldest museums in France, housed in a pavilion of the Place Stanislas
Important collection of European paintings
Includes a gallery dedicated to designer Jean Prouve and one to the Daum glass factory

w: Raised in the 18th century and still the seat of the Bishop of Nancy and Toul, this Baroque cathedral -- dedicated to Our Lady of the Annunciation and Saint Sigisbert -- holds national monument status, its restrained facade answering the gilded Place Stanislas just up the road.
s: An 18th-century Baroque seat of the Bishop of Nancy
_facts: Roman Catholic cathedral built in the 18th century, Baroque style
Dedicated to Our Lady of the Annunciation and Saint Sigisbert
National monument and seat of the Bishop of Nancy and Toul

w: Furniture designer Louis Majorelle commissioned architect Henri Sauvage to build this house and studio in 1901-1902 -- one of France's first and most influential Art Nouveau buildings, with contributions from ceramist Alexandre Bigot and glass artist Jacques Gruber. Now city-owned, it opens for tours by reservation.
s: Louis Majorelle's own Art Nouveau showcase home
_facts: Home and studio of furniture designer Louis Majorelle, built 1901-1902
Designed by architect Henri Sauvage; one of the first major Art Nouveau buildings in France
Contributions from ceramist Alexandre Bigot and stained-glass artist Jacques Gruber
Now city-owned, open certain days for tours by reservation

w: Emile Galle, Victor Prouve, Louis Majorelle, Antonin Daum and Eugene Vallin founded the Ecole de Nancy in 1901, and this 1964 museum -- set in patron Eugene Corbin's former house -- gathers their work under one roof, with a garden and aquarium pavilion. Nancy was one of Art Nouveau's great European centers.
s: The house-museum of Nancy's Art Nouveau movement
_facts: Devoted to the Ecole de Nancy, founded 1901 by Emile Galle, Victor Prouve, Louis Majorelle, Antonin Daum and Eugene Vallin
Museum opened 1964 in the former house of patron Eugene Corbin, architect Lucien Weissenburger
Includes a garden and an aquarium pavilion

w: Formerly the Opera de Nancy et de Lorraine, this company earned national-opera status in 2006 and now belongs to the Reunion des Operas de France, the European Network for Opera and Opera Europa. Its own orchestra accompanies every production inside a house that shares its address with the gilded Place Stanislas.
s: Lorraine's national opera house, on the royal square
_facts: Formerly named Opera de Nancy et de Lorraine; granted national-opera status in 2006
Member of Reunion des Operas de France, European Network For Opera and Opera Europa
All productions accompanied by its own Orchestra of the National Opera of Lorraine

w: Bishop Charles-Francois Turinaz, Canon Henri Blaise and architect Anthony Rougieux raised this basilica in Nancy's western Croix de Bourgogne district, blending Romanesque and Byzantine styles in deliberate homage to the Sacre-Coeur crowning Montmartre in Paris. It remains dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.
s: A Romanesque-Byzantine basilica modeled on Montmartre
_facts: Minor basilica combining Romanesque and Byzantine styles, inspired by the Sacre-Coeur of Montmartre in Paris
Built through Bishop Charles-Francois Turinaz, Canon Henri Blaise and architect Anthony Rougieux
Located in western Nancy, near the border with Laxou, in the Croix de Bourgogne area
Dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus

w: Stanislas Leszczynski, the last Duke of Lorraine and once King of Poland, chose this church as his resting place; a stone relief of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's arms still marks the clock tower above the door. Inside stands the 1505 statue of Our Lady of Good Help, carved by Mansuy Gauvain.
s: The exiled Polish king's chosen resting place
_facts: Historic church, formerly resting place of Stanislas Leszczynski, last Duke of Lorraine and King of Poland
Coat of arms of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth carved on the clock tower
Home to the 1505 statue of Our Lady of Good Help, sculpted by Mansuy Gauvain

w: Run jointly by the city and the University of Lorraine, this natural history museum pairs zoological and paleontological collections with three ground-floor aquariums -- the Nautilus, Calypso and Astrolabe galleries. Upstairs, a zoology gallery rounds out a collection built for scholars and the curious alike.
s: A two-storey natural history museum with live aquariums
_facts: Jointly managed by the Metropole du Grand Nancy and the University of Lorraine
Zoological, paleontological and living ichthyological collections across two storeys
Ground floor holds the Nautilus, Calypso and Astrolabe aquarium galleries plus a boat room and amphitheatre

w: Stanislas Leszczynski founded this garden in 1758 as an adjunct to the Royal College of Medicine, making it Nancy's oldest botanical garden. It stayed a working collection until 1993, when its plants moved to the larger Jardin botanique du Montet, later renamed for the 19th-century botanist who redesigned its beds.
s: Nancy's oldest garden, founded by an exiled king
_facts: Founded 1758 by Stanislas Leszczynski as an adjunct to the Royal College of Medicine
Nancy's oldest botanical garden, open daily and free
Active until 1993, when collections moved to the larger Jardin botanique du Montet
Named for botanist Dominique Alexandre Godron (1807-1880), who redesigned the garden

w: Architect Prosper Morey raised this basilica in the 19th century in the Rayonnant neo-Gothic style, its slender spire now one of the defining silhouettes of Nancy's old-town skyline. Tucked among the medieval streets near the Place Stanislas, a reminder the golden square wasn't the city's only chapter.
s: A neo-Gothic spire rising over Nancy's old town
_facts: Basilica built in the 19th century in the Rayonnant neo-Gothic style
Designed by architect Prosper Morey
